thread:
devops-bot: 🚨 Canary alert: canary pool ‘canary-042’ healthchecks failing. 1m 5xx rate = 7.4% (abort threshold 5%). Abort criteria triggered. Paging @anna (oncall).

anna (oncall): On it. Looking at metrics now — which rollout is this tied to?

liam (eng-runtime): That was v4.2.1 canary (gradual rollout) — started 02:15 UTC. Canary size 10 instances.

devops-bot: Canary rollout metadata: release_id=rel-2026-03-14-v4.2.1, strategy=canary(10), abort_on=5xx>5%/1m OR latency_p95>600ms.

anna (oncall): I see spikes on the request graph and a pile of 502/504s from gateway. Tail logs for one canary shard: ```2026-03-14T02:19:03Z ERROR handler: upstream write failed: broken pipe; stack: ...```

mike (sre): Can you grab canary instance IDs? I'll try to repro locally with same traffic profile.

liam (eng-runtime): Canary instances: canary-042-{a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,j}. Memory usage looks ok, but CPU on a couple nodes hit 95% at the same time as 5xx spike. Kernel OOM? No OOM logs.

anna (oncall): Any recent infra changes? autoscaling?

liam (eng-runtime): No infra changes. We shipped a change to request coalescing and a small update to the connection pool default (max_keepalive=20 -> 5) in v4.2.1. Suspect connection churn under burst traffic.

priya (product): Do we have evidence of customer impact yet? Which routes are failing?

anna (oncall): Early query: /v1/generate and streaming endpoints — elevated errors for a subset of customers. Approx 1.2k failing requests in the last 10m across canary nodes. Only traffic routed to canary instances is affected (traffic split 2%).

liam (eng-runtime): Given abort criteria and clear customer errors, I recommend immediate abort + revert to prior model variant. We should also flip the feature-flag kill-switch for the new connection logic as a quick mitigation. Anyone object?

mike (sre): Agreed. Prioritize rollback. I'll coordinate with deploy.

anna (oncall): Preparing to flip flag and trigger rollback. Command to kill-feature-flag: ```rk flag disable conn-pool-reduce-v4 --env=prod --scope=canary```

anna (oncall): Executing now.

deploy-bot: :gear: flag change recorded by anna (oncall). ID: flag-98321. Propagating to canary: 10/10 nodes acknowledged.

liam (eng-runtime): Nice — now kicking off canary rollback to rel-2026-03-13-v4.2.0. API: ```rk rollout abort --release rel-2026-03-14-v4.2.1 --scope=canary```

deploy-bot: Rollout abort initiated by liam (eng-runtime). rollback_job=rb-772. Status: in_progress.

anna (oncall): Watching error rate and latency. Metrics: 5xx down from 7.4% -> 2.1% within 2 minutes of flag flip (still trending).

mike (sre): I'm running a request profiler against canary-042-c which showed many `connection_reset_by_peer` around the same windows. Might be client-side connection drop due to keepalive change.

priya (product): Customer impact: we saw spikes in error rate for ~8 customers with high QPS routed through the canary split. Most errors were transient and retried by clients; a handful reported degraded UX. We should include initial affected-customer list in the incident ticket.

anna (oncall): Rollback job rb-772 reports: 6/10 canary nodes reverted. Continue monitoring.

liam (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR to revert the connection pool change in next patch and add a safer rollout gate. Also propose adding an integration test that simulates burst keepalive churn.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed. rb-772 status=success. Rel-back to rel-2026-03-13-v4.2.0 on all canary nodes.

anna (oncall): Confirming 5xx back to baseline 0.4% and p95 latency normalized. Customer-facing errors largely resolved.

mike (sre): Marking immediate mitigation successful. We'll keep canary flagged off for the next deploy until we have stress results.

priya (product): Noting impact to in-flight conversions for a few customers — follow-up with account owners needed. I'll draft customer outreach once we have root cause.

liam (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: connection pool size reduction had unintended interaction with upstream gateway under burst QPS causing connection resets and 5xx. Action items: revert code (PR #1447), add canary abort automation to also flip our flag when abort criteria hit, improve canary smoke tests.

anna (oncall): Creating incident: INC-2026-0314-01 with summary "canary abort during v4.2.1 rollout — connection pool change". Initial severity: Sev2. Linking metrics snapshots and logs: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/1712345678.

anna (oncall): Handoff to tom (next-oncall) in 20m. Tom — I'll leave list of commands, rollback job id, flag id, and links in the incident doc.

tom (next-oncall): Thanks, onboarding. Please DM if anything pops. I'll monitor follow-up PRs and verify QA stress results before unflagging.

devops-bot: Note: automated postmortem workflow started for INC-2026-0314-01. Owner assignment pending.

anna (oncall): Closing thread for active rollback mitigation. Will reopen if symptoms reappear. :white_check_mark:
